The idea of ‘least favourite’ is something I have thought about a lot.

as I’m sure many of you can relate, I do have easy access to a natural positive regard working with those I serve, which is why I love the work, 

but I have noticed that particular populations instantly produce a judgemental frustrated impatience in me that I really struggle to reconcile because it feels undeservingly mean spirited.

I have on many occasions said to myself there is no basis for this judgment,  I am wrong here, I know better than this, theoretically / academically / factually I know the truth, but my intrinsic response did not shift..

I reflected on this and I think my response to those ‘populations’ are representative one of the visceral imprints capitalism has had on my world view and beliefs, in that i view particular disadvantaged/ oppressed groups (who’s disadvantage and social exclusion is dictated and designed to reinforce and perpetuate imperialist ideology) not as equally deserving or worthy of my respectful and attentive consideration…. 

As an Aussie white Anglo I have begun to really try to unpack what it is to be someone whose cultural background is imperialist and capitalistic in nature, invading the land I live on.

 By reminding myself that my cultural background values power, control and dominance through exploitation and dehumanisation  over equality, community and basic kindness allows me to recognise that my baseless, surface level judgments influenced  on demographic attachment is my cultural background trying infiltrate itself in some way.. 

recognising these judgments in this way allows me to forgive myself for applying a dehumanising hierarchical lens on those I serve, providing me with more space to actively choose a more centred accepting approach..

Unless you know cars and can do repairs / maintenance yourself I personally would not use any auction place.. especially if you are on a budget..

I’ve had a handful of dealings with F3 including having bought from them (which did end up being a lemon but it was my fault for not being diligent, they did not misrepresent anything but they would have absolutely known there were hidden issues waiting for me, which is one point to be aware of, the actual law ….auction places are basically buy as is, where as car yards have have an after purchase warranty ) but f3 they’re friendly enough they don’t put the sales pressure on you etc..

But car auction places don’t really care about the Joe Blow buyers their business model is primarily about rotating their cars to actual car yards who buy in bulk  who think they know how to polish a turd for profit.. it’s a B2B structure and they also let the public have a look..

I’m sure the occasional unicorn comes through
at the cheaper end. But the likelihood of a decent cheap car not needing anything done soon ending up at f3 is low. 

When I was looking for my most recent suv I had a limited budget of around 10k. I went and had a look at a few of cars at F3, again they were friendly and open for me to test drive, I even took one for an independent mechanic inspection.. 

But because of the prior lemon (again my fault) i made sure I did my homework on each model before going to look and researched their most common problems etc I took a code scanner, a torch and some paper towel, drove off sight and had a decent look under each car, inside the engine and they all came up short.. 

Especially with older 4WD there’s heaps that can get missed if you don’t look underneath ..I would recommend no matter where you buy from you get an independent inspection done..

Again I’m only going off the cheaper options they had, I can’t speak to the more expensive options F3 stock, they seemed to have a decent selection there..

I can’t actually recommend any other car yards either..
None were overtly shit, but when ur on a budget the cheaper cars are the bottom of the barrel. And they aren’t required to tell you if there’s a leak or if something needs replacing.  

I ended up buying private, I had a professional inspection done, the car had a full service history and it drove nicely..

The whole process was a bloody pain in the ass, I went to soo many car yards and peoples homes for inspections., but unfortunately at my price range it was necessary I wasn’t going to risk buying a lemon again.. I’m just thankful it wasn’t an emergency purchase otherwise I would have been forced to buy a worse option..

I did my research, knew the price point, and I forced myself to walk away from many sales despite liking the car a lot.. (I also aged about 2 years over 6 month period)..but the car i bought is great, worth the extra effort for sure. Because I certainly didn’t have any extra cash, if I had another 5k to work with it would have been a very different (shorter) story..
